theme: The destination that surprised everyone — including us

linkedin.text:
Slide 1: The destination your team expects — vs. the one they can't stop talking about.

Slide 2: Problem → We default to the same cities. Safe, predictable, forgettable. Participants disengage before the program even starts.

Slide 3: Evidence → Across 1,500+ events and 130+ destinations, the highest-rated participant experiences consistently happen in places the group didn't see coming.

Slide 4: Evidence → Novelty isn't a nice-to-have. When people are somewhere genuinely new to them, attention goes up, conversations start, and the brand message lands differently.

Slide 5: Evidence → The destination brief we get most often: 'somewhere impressive but not generic.' That's not a vague ask — it's actually very answerable.

Slide 6: Conclusion → The right destination does real program work. It changes the dynamic before the first session starts.

Slide 7: Conclusion → Choosing a destination is a strategic decision, not a logistics one. It belongs in the same conversation as content and format.

Slide 8: What we do → At Uproduction Events, destination selection is part of the creative brief — not a checkbox after the concept is locked.

Slide 9: If you're scoping an incentive trip or executive retreat and want a candid read on what's working across different regions right now — DM me directly. No pitch, just a real conversation.

[Link in first comment]

instagram.text:
"I didn't think I'd care about the location. By day two I was asking when we could come back."

That's what a participant said after one of our incentive trips — and honestly, it's the best brief we could get before we start planning.

The destination isn't the backdrop. It's part of the program. We've built events across 130+ destinations and the ones that land hardest are almost never the most obvious ones.

Planning something for your team? Tell us the vibe you're going for — we'll tell you where in the world makes it happen. 👇

facebook.text:
We've worked in 130+ destinations. Some are obvious choices. Some surprise you completely — and end up being the ones participants talk about for years.

There's a specific kind of magic that happens when you take a group somewhere they didn't expect. The city does half your program for you. The novelty alone shifts the energy in the room — or the square, or the rooftop, or the vineyard.

We plan these moments for a living. If you're building a conference, incentive trip, or retreat and want a destination that actually earns its place in the program — drop a comment or send us a message. We'll tell you what's working right now.
